text:
sara: heads up — we're seeing a sudden latency tail in eu-central starting ~10:04 UTC. p50 fine, p95 and p99 jumping 2–4x. Noticed a spike in KV cache miss rate and memory pressure on several pods. :rotating_light:
raj: seeing same in the dashboard, traces point to runtime v2.7.1 that landed yesterday. Could be a cache eviction/regression. tagging eng-oncall. @marta can infra give a capacity snapshot?
marta: GPU pools in eu-central at 88% utilization, a few eviction alerts from the node agent. Autoscale attempted 6 new nodes but GCP quota throttled some launches — provisioning queues backfilled.
sara: can we throttle incoming traffic or divert region traffic to fallback? We should avoid cascading impact to us-west.
raj: putting traffic-shift plan in motion: shifting 30% of eu-central requests to eu-west & 20% to us-west for next 20m. Will update LB weights via rollout policy.
ops-bot: [action] Route update initiated: eu-central -> eu-west 30%, us-west 20% (manual override by raj)
kevin: runtime team investigating root cause — preliminary repro: increasing batch window results in higher cache churn and KV lru evictions when sequence lengths spike. Likely the batching change in commit a1b2c3 increased prefix concatenation, raising memory temp allocation.
lisa: can we temporarily disable the new batching heuristic? A quick rollback or feature flag flip would be ideal.
sara: if rollback is risky, we can apply emergency mitigation: reduce batch_window_ms from 25 to 5 and cap batch_size to 8 in eu-central only. That should reduce KV churn.
raj: doing partial config change now for eu-central nodes. Executing: 
```bash
redwoodctl clusters update eu-central --set runtime.batch_window_ms=5 --set runtime.max_batch_size=8 --selector=prod
```
deploy-bot: rollout started for cluster config update in eu-central. Canary on 3 pods.
kevin: also seeing increased cache miss rate in logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:03:54Z] kv_cache: miss key_prefix=conv:abc123 size=12
[2026-03-15T10:03:55Z] runtime: lru_evict count=47
```
marta: provisioning status: we freed two reserved GPU nodes and scaled pool by one low-priority instance (30s until ready). Quota request in flight for 8 more GPUs but unlikely in <15m.
lisa: as a temporary capacity savings step, we can route some traffic to quantized-8bit model variant to reduce memory footprint. Pros: fewer evictions; Cons: slight quality delta. Thoughts?
sara: yes do that for non-critical routes. Apply to search/rerank first, keep chat on full-precision.
raj: traffic shift + batch tweak + quantized fallback applied. Monitoring p95 now.
kevin: runtime rollback candidate prepared: revert commit a1b2c3 -> target v2.7.0. If mitigations don't stabilize within 12m we should roll back.
lisa: cost note — routing to on-demand and cross-region increases egress and instance costs. Estimated incremental spend ~$3.5k/hr if we keep current shift. Flagged to finance-runbook.
sara: fine for now, prioritize customer latency. Keep finance posted.
marta: request to SRE: reduce node eviction aggressiveness temporarily? Node agent has eviction.threshold=0.85, propose 0.92 for 10m to avoid flapping. Anyone object?
raj: agree for 10m, but monitor mem pressure.
ops-bot: [status] p95 latency eu-central 10m ago=210ms, now=590ms. After mitigations (10m) p95=230ms.
kevin: great — batch_window reduction looks to be the main win. Still watching KV miss rate for rebound.
sara: keep tracing hooks open for any customer errors. If rollback needed, coordinate planned window: 1772107800-1772107920 (15m).
lisa: creating a short post-incident cost/impact note template: link https://internal.redwood/incident-templates/quick-cost-run.md
raj: will run retrospective after incident closed. Thanks all for the quick ops. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident note appended to incident log: incident_id=INC-20260315-17, severity=SEV2, mitigation=traffic-shift+batch-tweak+quantized-fallback
